page: Microsoft Azure HB176-48rs_v4 belongs to the High Performance Computing HBv4 family running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The virtual machine provides 48 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning is notably dense, delivering 768 GB of total system RAM, which translates to an allocation of 16 GB per core. The instance includes a bundled 4355 GB local NVMe SSD for high-throughput temporary data and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent disk attachment. No discrete GPU accelerators are included.

The platform is engineered for distributed and high-throughput computing architectures, incorporating native RDMA capability to facilitate low-latency node-to-node communication across compute fabrics. The server assigns dedicated vCPU resources to prevent thread contention. Because it does not provision GPU hardware, it maintains qualitative resource efficiency for scenarios that require massive memory capacity and fast scratch disk without paying for idle accelerators. A notable configuration aspect is the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring private networking topologies or gateway routing for external access.

Given the elevated memory-to-core ratio, fast local NVMe SSD footprint, and RDMA interconnect support, the HB176-48rs_v4 instance is suited for memory-intensive simulation, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale ETL pipelines, and in-memory database caching.

Operating without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it relies on private networking and high-throughput interconnect capabilities. This configuration delivers an advantageous memory-to-core density alongside fast local scratch space, eliminating unnecessary GPU cost overhead for compute tasks that are strictly memory and storage bound. It is tailored for memory-intensive high-performance computing workloads, large-scale data processing pipelines, scientific modeling, and in-memory analytics.
